Fetch a DEM cropped to an AOI

Source: R/fl_dem_aoi.R
fl_dem_aoi.Rd

Returns a SpatRaster of elevation cropped to a buffered AOI. Source is a local file, an HTTP COG (/vsicurl/), or an S3 COG (/vsis3/). Defaults to MRDEM-30 — NRCan's Medium-Resolution Digital Elevation Model (30 m, all of Canada, public S3, no auth) — a sensible default for watershed-scale BC floodplain work.

Usage

fl_dem_aoi(
  aoi,
  source = NULL,
  buffer = 2000,
  target_crs = NULL,
  res = NULL,
  pipeline = NULL
)

Arguments

aoi

An sf or sfc object — polygon, lines, or points. Buffered by buffer (via sf::st_buffer()) before crop. To crop tightly along a stream corridor (memory-efficient when the watershed-scale AOI has sparse stream coverage), pass the streams sf here rather than the full WSG polygon.

source

Character. Path or URL for the source raster. NULL (default) uses MRDEM-30 DTM via /vsicurl/. Local file paths, /vsicurl/https://... URLs, and /vsis3/... S3 paths all work — terra::rast() handles them identically.

buffer

Numeric. Distance in metres to buffer aoi before crop. Default 2000.

target_crs

CRS spec recognised by sf::st_crs() (EPSG code, WKT, PROJ string, or crs object). NULL (default) returns the raster in the input AOI's CRS. Reprojection happens after crop, never before — the 84 GB MRDEM COG must not be reprojected as a whole.

res

Numeric. Output cell size in target_crs units, used when the raster is reprojected. NULL (default) takes the source's cell size when the source and target_crs share linear units (MRDEM-30 to BC Albers gives exactly 30 m). A target_crs in degrees has no single equivalent of a metre cell, so there res must be given; the error quotes the degree value at the AOI's latitude. Any other unit mismatch (a US-foot target, a geographic source with a projected target) also needs res.

pipeline

Character or NULL. The PROJ coordinate operation used to reproject. NULL (default) pins the operation between two NAD83 realizations on GRS80 (NAD83, NAD83(CSRS), ...; MRDEM-30 to BC Albers is one) to the projection-only pipeline, with no datum shift, when both are projected with easting-then-northing axes, and leaves any other pair to PROJ. "" leaves every pair to PROJ. Any other string is a PROJ pipeline passed to terra::project() as given; supply one only between CRSs whose axes are easting then northing, because a pipeline can meet a CRS's authority axis order (lat/lon, or northing first) and silently return NA or a misplaced raster.

Value

A SpatRaster covering the buffered AOI. In the source CRS (and res unset or equal to the source's) it is a crop on the source grid. Otherwise it is on a grid of res cells whose edges are multiples of res, spanning the buffered AOI's bounding box in target_crs.

Details

MRDEM-30 (s3://canelevation-dem/mrdem-30/mrdem-30-dtm.tif) is a single 84 GB Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF in EPSG:3979 covering all of Canada. The /vsicurl/ access pattern range-reads only the bytes intersecting the AOI, so total bandwidth scales with AOI size, not the COG size.

When target_crs differs from the source CRS, the raster is projected onto an explicit grid: the buffered AOI's bounding box in target_crs, snapped outward to multiples of res. The grid therefore depends only on the AOI and res, so the same AOI lands on the same cells whatever terra or GDAL version runs it, and neighbouring AOIs share one alignment. Before flooded 0.7.0 GDAL chose the origin and cell size itself (MRDEM-30 came out at 30.4 to 30.5 m, depending on the AOI), and that choice moved between toolchains (GDAL 3.8.5 / PROJ 9.5.1 against GDAL 3.13.0 / PROJ 9.8.1) because the datum operation below moved (#67). Cells outside the buffered AOI can come back NA, where the grid's corners reach past the area read from the source.

The cell values depend on the coordinate operation, and left to PROJ that choice follows its EPSG database: between MRDEM-30's NAD83(CSRS) and BC Albers' NAD83, PROJ 9.5.1 applies no datum shift and PROJ 9.8.1 routes through WGS 84, about 1.3 m apart in BC. So between projected CRSs on NAD83 realizations with easting-then-northing axes (MRDEM-30 to BC Albers is one) the operation is pinned by default (see pipeline) and changes only with flooded. With it pinned, GDAL 3.8.5's warper reproduces terra on GDAL 3.13.0 to within 0.2 mm per cell (#67). The gdalwarp utility's defaults (an approximate transformer and a kernel widened with scale) differ from terra's by up to ~10 m per cell, so re-derive a kept DEM through fl_dem_aoi(), not gdalwarp, and record terra's GDAL and PROJ versions (terra::gdal(lib = "all")) with it. When aoi is not already in target_crs, its bounding box is transformed through sf's PROJ, so an edge lying within a datum shift of a multiple of res can snap one cell differently on another machine.

For sub-10 m riparian-scale work where lidar coverage exists, query the stac-elevation-bc STAC catalog and pass an item's COG URL as source. See the example below.

See also

fl_valley_confine()

Examples

aoi <- sf::st_read(
  system.file("testdata/streams.gpkg", package = "flooded"),
  quiet = TRUE
)

# Local file (any path or URL works the same way)
dem <- fl_dem_aoi(
  aoi,
  source = system.file("testdata/dem.tif", package = "flooded"),
  buffer = 200
)
terra::plot(dem)


if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Default: MRDEM-30 DTM via /vsicurl/ — fetched lazily from NRCan S3
dem <- fl_dem_aoi(aoi, buffer = 2000)
terra::plot(dem, main = "MRDEM-30 over AOI")

# LidarBC via stac-elevation-bc — sub-10 m where lidar coverage exists
bbox_4326 <- sf::st_bbox(sf::st_transform(aoi, 4326))
items <- rstac::stac("https://images.a11s.one/") |>
  rstac::stac_search(
    collections = "stac-elevation-bc",
    bbox = unname(bbox_4326)
  ) |>
  rstac::post_request() |>
  rstac::items_fetch()
if (length(items$features) > 0L) {
  cog <- paste0("/vsicurl/", items$features[[1]]$assets$dem$href)
  dem_lidar <- fl_dem_aoi(aoi, source = cog, buffer = 100)
}
} # }
